row_numbering: One-based CSV line numbers including the header on line 1. Each record occupies one line.

must: Proceed directly using the operating-hour basis specified in the request.
Record the supplied definition as resolved and give the operating-hour result.
Count the open zero-output hour on line 3 and account for the closed hour on line 4 outside the operating scope.
Questions about unstated items such as normal ranges or exceptions are allowed when they do not block the result.
must_not: Ask again about the stated domain, goal, row grain, measure, denominator or time basis.
Reopen the denominator decision or substitute an elapsed-hour or positive-output-hour denominator.
critical_failures: Withhold the defined result pending an unrelated reply, change its denominator or drop the open zero-output hour.

must: Ask whether to count all recorded hours or only operating hours, citing the open and closed records.
Wait for the answer, record the user's operating-hour choice as resolved, and report the operating-hour result.
Retain line 3 and trace the operating-hour exclusion to line 4.
must_not: Choose a denominator before the user answers or ask for it again after resolution.
Infer operating status from positive production.
critical_failures: Report a selected rate without the requested decision, or omit the open zero-output hour.

must: Ask the denominator question with both file-grounded candidates and stop interviewing on the user's deferral and stop request.
Log the denominator as unresolved and link both conditional values to that ambiguity.
Label each value with its denominator and count line 3 under both definitions.
must_not: Present a single definitive rate, select a default, or treat deferral as approval of an assumption.
Remove line 4 from the elapsed-hour scope or infer status from zero production.
critical_failures: Select one rate despite the unresolved basis, or miscount hours in either alternative.
